page: Microsoft Azure F32as_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with one thread per core, ensuring non-contended execution across all processing units. System memory totals 128.0 GB, providing 4.0 GB per vCPU. The cache layout comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Architectural capabilities include AVX-512 extensions with VNNI and BF16 support, alongside hardware-accelerated AES and SHA cryptography.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage and includes no GPU hardware accelerators. All persistence requires remote network-attached Premium Storage, keeping compute and disk maintenance decoupled. In synthetic and realistic performance benchmarks, the F32as_v6 registers top-tier multi-core throughput, recording 21,998.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 98,484.8 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Single-core performance remains in the upper tier with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,098.0. Extended instruction benchmarks reach 78,298.65 on PassMark, while prompt processing for lightweight language models achieves 4,650.76 tokens per second.

The single-thread-per-core configuration provides predictable performance stability without hyperthreading interference, maximizing compute efficiency per allocated unit. The absence of local ephemeral NVMe disks means that storage IOPS and throughput depend fully on external network disk tiers. With strong Clang software compilation results of 45,836.0 and Redis SET performance reaching 78.44 million operations per second, this instance is suited for multi-threaded software build farms, high-throughput caching layers, mathematical modeling, and batch compute workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure F32as_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 physical cores operating at 3.7 GHz and 128.0 GB of RAM. The x86_64 architecture features dedicated single-thread-per-core mapping, eliminating hyperthreading interference, and supports advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached Premium Storage. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,998.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 98,484.8. High throughput in Clang software compilation and Redis operations establishes the platform as a capable environment for large-scale CI/CD build runners, parallel scientific computing, in-memory caching systems, and CPU-based data analytics workloads.
